item.title: PIAA WRESTLING: Hazleton Area’s Gabe Benyo advances to final
item.description: HERSHEY — Gabe Benyo wasn’t happy with the way he wrestled Thursday night. The Hazleton Area sophomore showed sometimes all you have to do is survive and advance. item.title: PIAA CLASS 4A BOYS: Doherty lifts Prep into second round; Valley View moves on
item.description: SCRANTON – Packy Doherty drained his final shot inside of the Xavier Center as the horn sounded to sub him out. With the Scranton Prep student section shouting and chanting his name, the Cavalier took a moment to soak it all in. One final time. One final moment inside a gym where he reigned supreme the last four seasons. item.title: PIAA GIRLS’ BASKETBALL: Lady Cougars cruise past Garnet Valley in Class 6A opener
item.description: Hazleton eased past short-handed Garnet Valley, 71-34, in the first round of the PIAA Class 6A tournament on Friday evening at Hughie McGeehan Gymnasium.

item.title: PIAA BASKETBALL: Wyoming Seminary holds off Muncy to advance in state tournament
item.description: MUNCY — When what was once a 14-point fourth-quarter lead dwindled to three late in the fourth quarter, Wyoming Seminary didn’t panic. When leading scorer Ella Stambaugh fouled out with 2:39 left in the game and the Blue Knights were holding on to that three-point lead, the mood never changed. item.title: PIAA BOYS BASKETBALL: Dallas, Crestwood move to second round
item.description: NEW TRIPOLI — Dallas took a two-point lead into the locker room Friday night in its PIAA Class 4A boys basketball first-round game against Northwestern Lehigh. The Mountaineers kept expanding on it in the second half. Dallas outscored Northwestern Lehigh by one in the third quarter, and used an 18-13 edge in the fourth quarter to pull away for the 57-48 victory over the District 11 runner-up to advance to Tuesday’s second round. item.title: COLLEGE ROUNDUP: Misericordia pulls away late to close trip
item.description: FORT PIERCE, Fla. – Misericordia baseball trailed 2-0 most of the game Friday, but exploded for a combined 10 runs in the seventh and eighth innings for a 10-2 win over Heidelberg University on the final day of the team’s spring-break trip in Florida. The Cougars, now 6-5, ended the trip with two wins after an 8-3 win over Alvernia on Thursday.
